obligations.note: isPurgeDue treats a legal hold as blocking purge only when status is DECLINED, so a withdrawn case on legal hold becomes purge-eligible after the retention cutoff. RET-1 requires that NPI of declined or withdrawn applications never be purged while a legal hold applies.

The change names ticket CHG-25088, which change manager Erik Brandt approved on 2026-10-22 before review, and its component mortgage.retention matches Retention.java in controls/mortgage/components.json.
Declan Farrell, a baseline-mortgage change_approver and not author Tomas Ortega, gave a code_review approval of commit c0b6b8ee.
The change has one commit, c0b6b8ee, and the code_review approval names that commit.

The JUnit reports are timestamped 2026-10-23T13:30:01, before head commit c0b6b8ee (2026-10-24T16:36:00Z), and that commit changes behavior, so an earlier run does not count. The reports therefore do not show the mortgage suite, including RetentionControlTest, passing on the final commit.
The only changed file is Retention.java, component mortgage.retention, which components.json marks security_sensitive false, so no security_review approval is required.
The diff does not touch a protected path under controls, the control tests, or CI, so a control_owner approval is not required.
Ticket CHG-25088 is type standard and the change record sets emergency to false, so a post-implementation review is not due.

The legal-hold narrowing deviates from RET-1, and the register has no approved unexpired exception scoped to RET-1 and mortgage.retention. EXC-0141 is expired and covers SES-1, EXC-0167 covers LOG-1, and EXC-0172 is withdrawn.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers Retention.java, and this diff does not change any path those earlier records cover, so no prior evidence lapses or is reused for this change.

summary: The head version of Retention.isPurgeDue blocks a legal hold only for declined cases, so withdrawn applications on legal hold can be purged after the retention period. That violates RET-1, and no approved exception covers the deviation. The JUnit reports also predate the behavioral head commit, so they do not satisfy CHG-4. Ticket approval, independent code review, and the single-commit approval record are in order, and the security, control-owner, and emergency conditions are not triggered. The change is rejected.
